title: Enums, tuples, and indexers
hook: Not every type needs a named class. Enums name discrete values. Tuples name a bag of values without a type declaration. Indexers make a type look like an array or dictionary at the call site.

sections.heading: Enums
sections.prose: An enum is a named integer. The default underlying type is int. [Flags] enums combine bits; ToString and HasFlag are the usual tools. Never trust an enum deserialized from JSON or a CSV column without checking Enum.IsDefined or a switch that has a default — numeric values can be out of range and still type-check as the enum. Prefer enum for closed sets (SQS message kind, auth provider) and classes/records for anything with behavior.

sections.heading: Tuples and deconstruction
sections.prose: ValueTuple (the (string id, int score) syntax) is a struct with Item1-style fields plus optional names that are mostly compile-time sugar. Tuples are excellent as private method returns and terrible as public API: names vanish across assemblies more easily than you expect, and you cannot add validation. Deconstruction (var (id, score) = row) works on tuples and on types that expose Deconstruct methods. Anonymous types still exist; new code prefers tuples or records.

snippets.label: Enum, tuple return, and indexer
snippets.explanation: Parse returns a tuple for a private helper. HeaderMap exposes an indexer like a dictionary without leaking the field. AuthProvider stays a closed set.

sections.heading: Indexers
sections.prose: An indexer is a parameterized property named this[...]. You can overload indexers on parameter type. They compile to get_Item/set_Item methods. Use them for collection-like types, not for random lookup APIs where a named method is clearer. Range and index types (^1, 1..3) show up on Span and collections (modules 08 and 17).

interviewTakeaways: Enums are integers with names; out-of-range values exist.
Tuples are lightweight returns, not public contracts.
commonPitfalls: Public APIs returning (string, string, string) instead of a record.
Switching on enum without a default for unknown numeric values.

jsTsCorrelations.note: TS string unions are often a better model than numeric enums. C# enums are real CLR types; TS enums may emit objects or disappear depending on settings.
JS destructuring works on objects and arrays. C# deconstruction is an opt-in protocol (Deconstruct) plus tuple syntax.
